messages.text: qq can i mind bitcoin via kryptex with hammer miner bc04 seems to not like it connection is great not mining shares like it should
Handed to the team · Can't confirm Kryptex SHA-256 ASIC compatibility from product facts; needs JD.

Most likely cause: Kryptex is built around GPU and CPU algorithms, so a SHA-256 ASIC pointed at it often connects on the socket but never gets accepted work. Quickest test is a plain SHA-256 stratum pool with your BTC worker name, and see if shares start landing. If they do, it's Kryptex, not the BC04.

I've pinged JD on our side to confirm the exact Kryptex setup for these units. Stay in the chat, he'll jump in here.

One thing: what worker and password string are you using?
(contact hidden), 12345

That's the usual culprit. On SHA-256 pools the worker field normally has to be your account or BTC payout address first, then the rig name, like yourbtcaddress.(contact hidden), with the password just x. A bare rig name with no account in front connects fine and then never gets credited work, which matches exactly what you're seeing.

Try it that way on a standard pool first. JD will confirm the Kryptex-specific format when he's in here.
i have like that miss spoke i cleared the PW to only x.

Then the next thing to rule out is the pool itself. Point the BC04 at a known SHA-256 stratum endpoint for ten minutes and watch the share counter. If shares land there, the BC04 and your network are fine and the problem is on the Kryptex side, which is what I suspect given it's built around GPU algorithms.

JD's the one who can confirm whether Kryptex serves SHA-256 work at all. He's been pinged and will pick this up here.

Does the miner's own dashboard show any accepted shares, or a flat zero?

Flat zero with a good connection almost always means the pool is handing out work the chip can't use, not a hardware fault. That's the Kryptex mismatch pattern.

Swap the pool to a plain SHA-256 stratum endpoint, keep the same worker format, restart the miner and give it ten minutes. If shares start counting, you have your answer and you know the unit is healthy.

JD has this and will confirm the Kryptex side here shortly. What's the hashrate the dashboard is reporting while it's connected?
will try it 1 sec.
Take your time, I'm here.
if it doesn't work i'll like a return or switch these out to the most compatible qaxes/or strongest bit axe.
Searched the catalog · NerdQaxe NerdOctaxe Bitaxe

Honestly, a different unit probably won't fix this. Every SHA-256 miner we sell talks the same stratum, so if Kryptex isn't feeding the BC04 work, it won't feed a NerdQX or an Octaxe either. Let's see the pool test first.

If the BC04 turns out faulty, that's an RMA, not a swap, and returns on a shipped unit go through the team. Was it overclocked at any point?
i have several qaxe's and bitaxe online currently sorry i'm running fine on my other rigs.

That changes it. If those rigs are on Kryptex too, then the pool does serve SHA-256 work and the problem is local to the BC04, config or the unit itself.

Are your working rigs pointed at the same Kryptex URL and port? If so, copy that exact stratum string and port into the BC04, change only the worker suffix, and restart it. A wrong port is the usual difference between a rig that hashes and one that just connects.
yes all of them are. i'll try the 2nd rig here tonite. i haven't un boxed it.

Good test. Same settings on the second BC04 tells you straight away whether it's the unit or the config. If the new one hashes and the first still sits at zero, that first one is a hardware case and JD will take it from there.

Worth noting the firmware version on both while you're in there, in case they shipped on different builds.

Come back here when you've run it.
thx.
Used the chat-interview skill
Before you go, one thing: you've got several Qaxes and Bitaxes running, so what made you add the BC04 to the mix?
becuase the larger octaxe was out of stock when i purchase these as a swap
So the BC04s were the fallback, not the first pick. What was it about the Octaxe you wanted that the smaller units don't give you?
lesson learned stick with what works
Fair enough, thanks for telling me. Run the second unit tonight and come back here with what it does, and JD will pick up the faulty one if it comes to that.
good news so far firmware update needed and i went back to original bit coin pool with kryptex..getting 1 hash currently better than before.

That's the fix then, stale firmware. Shares landing at all means the chip is getting real work.

Give it an hour before you judge the rate. The dashboard average climbs slowly from cold and the first few shares skew it. If it's still crawling well under 6 TH/s after that, tell me and JD will look at it.

Worth flashing the second one before you set it up.
yes 2 now thx for the support.

Nice, both hashing. Glad it was just firmware.

A copy of this chat goes to your email once we're done, so the settings are there if you need them again.
only for now i got buzy but the one causing issues is working fine i see it on my kryptex acct mining away thank you.

Great, showing up on the Kryptex side is the real confirmation. Go get on with your day.

If anything wobbles on either unit, come back here and we'll pick it up.
thank you GN.
Goodnight, and happy hashing.
